summary: Session affinity reset after model promote causes pinned sessions to route to canary during rollout
description:
Issue summary: Several customer sessions pinned to model redwood-13b-v2 observed abrupt routing to a canary variant immediately after a model 'promote' operation as part of a controlled rollout. This caused degraded response quality for a subset of sessions and confusion in client telemetry.

Impact: Approximately 3% of active sessions for Lexicon Health (dedicated cluster) received canary model responses for 6-12 minutes during the promote operation. Customer reports user-facing quality regressions and discrepant logs. No 5xx errors reported, but incorrect model served for pinned sessions violates pinning guarantees.

Environment: prod/us-east, Dedicated pool dh-prod-lexicon-01, promote executed from Console -> Rollouts at 2026-03-10T15:12:00Z. Autoscaling was idle, no spot evictions.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer has long-lived chat sessions pinned to redwood-13b-v2 via session pinning API.
2) Operator executes model promote (promote canary to stable) through Console rollout UI with 10% canary weight and then finalize promote to 100%.
3) During finalize, routing table update and route cache invalidation are applied.
4) Approximately at the finalization step, a subset of pinned sessions lost affinity and began hitting canary variant for first request after a short TTL refresh.

Logs & evidence:
- Router traces (trace IDs): rtr-20260310-7a9f, rtr-20260310-7b02 show session_id and old_pin -> routed_model mismatch.
- Console rollout audit: rollout-lexicon-20260310 promoted canary redwood-13b-v2-canary -> redwood-13b-v2 at 2026-03-10T15:13:05Z.
- Customer telemetry: client session logs show pinned_model = redwood-13b-v2 but received_model = redwood-13b-v2-canary for first post-promote request.

Initial hypothesis: During the promote path we trigger a full route cache refresh that races with the session-affinity refresher. Session-affinity metadata for long-lived sessions has a short TTL refresh that was re-evaluated during the same window and incorrectly re-bound to the newly minted canary alias because the route rewrite stage used a transient alias map before old pin anchors were re-applied. Another contributing factor could be inconsistent ordering between router config push and affinity rehydration job on dedicated nodes.

Temporary mitigation provided: Instructed customer to pin by explicit model_id (stable): POST /v1/sessions/{id}/pin {"model_id": "redwood-13b-v2@20260307"} which restored expected routing for affected sessions. Also applied console hold on rollout finalize to prevent re-run.

Requested outcome: Patch to make promote path maintain pin invariants (either block affinity refreshes during promote finalization or apply atomic alias mapping that preserves explicit model_id pins).

investigation_notes: Checked router and affinity refresher logs across dedicated pool nodes: discovered out-of-order config timestamps on node dh-prod-lexicon-01-03 at 2026-03-10T15:12:58Z.

Affinity refresher performs a TTL refresh every 60s and will rebind to whatever alias mapping is visible; promote finalization applied alias swap at 15:13:05Z, which overlapped with refresher window leading to transient rebind.

Staging reproduction: created 500 sessions pinned to previous model alias, executed promote flow; ~2.8% sessions experienced rebind within first 10s after finalize. Correlated with config propagation latency between router and scheduler (~200-400ms).
Existing guardrails (promote with hold) prevented mass misroutes but did not cover long-lived session affinity refresh edge cases.
Related config: router uses in-memory alias map with eventual consistency across nodes; consider atomic alias map swap or versioned pin resolution with precedence for explicit model_id pins.
resolution: Workaround: customer applied explicit model_id pin; support recommended holding rollout finalize during peak. Engineering implemented PR #482 to sequence alias map push ahead of affinity refresh and added a 30s affinity-lock window during promote finalization. PR merged to main 2026-03-13; will be deployed to dedicated clusters during next maintenance window. Added e2e regression test for long-lived session pin preservation. Follow-up: schedule post-deploy verification with Lexicon Health and update rollout runbook to include affinity-lock step.
